verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every constant of (6.2) is in the repository with the same value, but spread over three files and with one notation inlined. Exact matches: J_g (cover x = (3x₁+x₂, x₁+5x₂), i.e. the matrix [[3,1],[1,5]] on column vectors), Λ_g = 4 − √2 (Lambda), T_g = 4 + √2 (coverGrowth), ρ_g = log Λ_g / log T_g (rho), κ_s = 10⁻⁵ (kappa = 1/100000), d_r = 2((1+h)ρ_g − hκ_s) (radialExponent). The only encoding difference: b_g = √2 − 1 has no declaration of its own; it occurs inlined inside the two direction vectors, radialDirection = (1, 1 − √2) = (1, −b_g) and timeDirection = (√2 − 1, 1) = (b_g, 1), so the rewriting is substitution of the literal. The inequality d_r > 0 is radialExponent_pos, proved under 0 ≤ h, which contains the paper's range 0 < h < 1/2 (the Lean docstring says so). The eigenvector identities the paper asserts just after (6.2), J_g v_r = Λ_g v_r and J_g v_t = T_g v_t, are cover_radialDirection and cover_timeDirection. Of the chain 1 < Λ_g < T_g asserted in the same sentence, the separate bounds 2 < Λ_g (Lambda_two_lt, which gives 1 < Λ_g) and 1 < T_g (Tg_one_lt) are stated; a declaration stating Λ_g < T_g was not found.
